title: StockSmart Billing Standard — Quantity of the First Customer-Owned Fill of a Converted Bin on Credit Hold
content:
This billing standard of the StockSmart Vendor-Managed Inventory Program fixes how many units the first customer-owned fill of a bin converted from consignment takes while the customer's Commercial Credit Account is on hold.

**1. The bin.** The converted item is the item of the program's most recent consignment withdrawal, and the bin's fill-to level is the highest fill-to level among its entries of their latest date; where there is no consignment withdrawal or two or more carry that most recent date, where there is no service visit or two or more carry the latest visit date, or where the bin has no entry, no fill is booked under this standard. A consignment withdrawal counts as a par-review conversion only where the converted item's bin carries no removal entry and the program is not closed; after a withdrawal that follows the removal of the bin or the end of the program, no fill is booked under this standard. The fill is the bin's first customer-owned fill only while no replenishment line of the converted item has been booked on the program; once one has, the bin is outside this standard.

**2. The program and the account.** The fill is booked under this standard only on a program whose status is active or terminating, whose tier's credit hold service rule is critical items only, while the customer's Commercial Credit Account is on hold, and where the bin's entries of their latest date include one flagging it critical.

**3. The price line.** The item's latest price line is its price line in the customer's Contract Pricing Agreement with the latest effective date, and its kind is that line's event: an addition, a repricing or a removal. A customer with no pricing agreement on record is outside this standard, and so is an item with no price line in the customer's agreement, with a price line that takes effect after today (every line of the item must be dated today or within the 1200 months before it), or with two price lines of its latest effective date, and so is an item whose latest price line is a removal where the agreement is cost-plus, discounts the item's category, honours list quantity breaks, or the item is booked at the ship-to as a non-stock special order.

**4. The calculation.** The fill price is the list price on the item's latest price line less the list discount percent of the customer's pricing agreement, rounded half up to 4 decimal places; the allowance share is the whole, 1, and no release is added (0.00). The allowance left is worked out in this order: the tier's critical item replenishment cap is multiplied by the allowance share, every release added is added to that product, and the value of critical replenishment already delivered at the same visit is subtracted; the fill is the lesser of the bin's fill-to level and the whole units the allowance left buys at the fill price, taken to six decimal places and rounded down, never below zero.

### Worked figures (hypothetical tier cap, prices and bins)

| Cap | Already delivered critical at the visit | Allowance left | List price; list discount | Fill price | Units bought | Fill-to level | Fill |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1000.00 | 400.00 | 600.00 | 50.00; 20 percent | 40.0000 | 15 | 24 | 15 |
| 1000.00 | 400.00 | 600.00 | 50.00; 20 percent | 40.0000 | 15 | 10 | 10 |
| 1000.00 | 0.00 | 1000.00 | 33.33; 15 percent | 28.3305 | 35.297647, rounded down to 35 | 60 | 35 |
| 1000.00 | 1100.00 | below zero | 50.00; 20 percent | 40.0000 | 0 | 24 | 0 |

The visit is the program's latest service visit; the value already delivered is the value of the replenishment lines flagged critical booked at that visit.
